extracted.intended_audience: neuroscientists and cognitive neuroscientists conducting fMRI studies of aesthetic experience (neuroesthetics)
extracted.subtask_description: Design, conduct, and analyze an fMRI experiment measuring neural correlates of perceived beauty of mathematical formulae in mathematician participants, including behavioral ratings (beauty and understanding), stimulus balancing, scanning parameters, and statistical inference procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participant selection and exclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Sixteen mathematicians (3 females, age range 22–32 years, 1 left-handed) at postgraduate or postdoctoral level, recruited from colleges in London; all had normal or corrected to normal vision. One subject was eliminated after it transpired he suffered from attention deficit hyperactivity disorder and had been on medication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recruit expert participants appropriate to the stimulus domain (here, advanced mathematicians). Screen for confounding medical/medication conditions and exclude if necessary; report demographics (sex, age range, handedness) and vision status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics and consent
rubrics_metrics.description: All gave written informed consent and the study was approved by the Ethics Committee of University College London.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obtain institutional ethics approval and written informed consent; report these explicitly in methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stimulus set and pre-scan beauty ratings
rubrics_metrics.description: Each subject was given 60 mathematical formulae about 2–3 weeks before scanning to study at leisure and to rate on a scale of −5 (Ugly) to +5 (Beautiful).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect pre-scan beauty ratings to identify individually preferred and non-preferred stimuli and to use for stimulus balancing/pseudo-randomization during scanning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scan-time beauty rating categories
rubrics_metrics.description: During scanning subjects re-rated the same equations on an abridged scale of Ugly—Neutral—Beautiful (three categories).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a simpler in-scanner rating scale to reduce task complexity and enable interactive button responses; ensure mapping of categories to numeric codes for analysis (authors coded Ugly=−1, Neutral=0, Beautiful=+1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-scan understanding ratings
rubrics_metrics.description: A few days after scanning, subjects reported their level of understanding of each equation on a numerical scale from 0 (no understanding) to 3 (profound understanding) and gave subjective feelings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect post-scan comprehension/understanding measures to dissociate cognitive understanding from aesthetic ratings; use an ordinal scale (here 0–3) and include qualitative questions about subjective emotional responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of pre-scan ratings to balance/pseudo-randomize stimuli
rubrics_metrics.description: Pre-scan ratings were used to divide the 60 equations into three groups; 20 'low' rated, 20 'medium' rated, and 20 'high' rated equations for each subject. The sequence was organized so that 5 low-, 5 medium- and 5 highly-rated equations appeared in each functional session, and a low-rated equation was never followed by another low-rated equation (similarly for medium and high).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance stimulus presentation across sessions per participant to achieve roughly equal representation of rating levels and avoid successive same-category trials; pseudo-randomize to prevent order effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trial timing and baseline acquisition
rubrics_metrics.description: Each session started with a blank gray screen for 19.5 s; 15 trials per session each with an equation displayed for 16 s, blanks and response periods as described, and four baseline blanks of 16–17 s inserted between trials; sessions ended with a 30 s blank.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define explicit timing for stimulus presentation, inter-trial intervals, response windows, and baseline periods to allow reliable BOLD baseline estimates and T1 equilibration; document durations precisely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stimulus visual properties and presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Equations displayed in same sized font in white on a uniform mid-gray background; overall screen brightness and equation visual angles specified (width 4°–24°, height 1°–5°); display resolution and refresh rate provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Control and report display properties (font, colors with colorimetric values if possible, background luminance, visual angles, resolution and refresh rate) to ensure reproducibility and control low-level perceptual confounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: In-scanner response collection
rubrics_metrics.description: During a 3 s response screen the subject selected a scan-time beauty rating (Beautiful, Neutral, or Ugly) by pressing keypad buttons; their selection was interactively displayed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide an interactive response window with clear mapping from button to category and on-screen feedback; choose a short response window compatible with the design and the cognitive load.

rubrics_metrics.name: fMRI acquisition parameters and coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Scans acquired on a 3-T Siemens Magnetom Trio with a 32-channel head coil; B0 fieldmap acquired with double-echo FLASH; EPI sequence measured BOLD signals with 48 axial slices, 2 mm thickness, 1 mm gap, voxel resolution ~3×3×3 mm covering nearly whole brain; high-resolution T1 (MDEFT) anatomical scans (176 slices, 1 mm isotropic).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report scanner make/model, coil, fieldmap sequence, EPI parameters (slice count, thickness, gap, voxel size, coverage), and anatomical acquisition parameters to allow replication and interpretation of sensitivity/coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preprocessing and analysis software
rubrics_metrics.description: SPM8 (Statistical Parametric Mapping) was used to analyze the results, as in previous studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify analysis package and version; follow established preprocessing pipelines and reference prior work when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single-subject model: parametric modulators and orthogonalization
rubrics_metrics.description: At the single-subject level the understanding rating (0–3) and the scan-time beauty rating (coded as −1 for 'Ugly', 0 for 'Neutral', and +1 for 'Beautiful') for each equation were included as first and second parametric modulators of a boxcar function modeling the appearance of each equation. Because of SPM orthogonalization, the beauty parametric modulator captures variance that cannot be explained by the understanding rating (and vice versa when order reversed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use parametric modulators to model graded subjective variables; carefully order modulators and understand orthogonalization behavior to isolate variance uniquely attributable to each predictor. Consider running analyses with modulators in both orders to isolate 'beauty-only' and 'understanding-only' effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parametric versus categorical analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: A parametric analysis looks for a relationship between BOLD signal and differences in the rated quantity on an individual session basis; a categorical analysis will average the BOLD signal for each category of the rated quantity over all sessions and subjects. Orthogonalization of two parametric regressors is available in parametric analysis but not in categorical analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer parametric analyses when modeling continuous/graded behavioral measures and when isolation via orthogonalization is required; use categorical analyses to obtain parameter estimates for discrete categories but note reduced sensitivity and lack of orthogonalization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling imbalance in condition counts
rubrics_metrics.description: There were fewer 'Ugly' rated equations than 'Neutral' or 'Beautiful' and in two sessions there was no 'Ugly' rating. This imbalance does not bias the estimation of, or inference about, the effects of beauty—it only reduces the efficiency with which the effects can be estimated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Imbalanced condition counts reduce statistical efficiency; report imbalance and justify that estimation remains possible; design to minimize extreme imbalance where feasible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Second-level (group) analysis and random effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Contrast images for each subject for the parametric beauty rating and for All equations vs. Baseline were taken to a 2nd-level (random effects) analysis. One-sample t-tests (df=14) were used at the group level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use random-effects group analysis to enable population-level inference; state the second-level tests and degrees of freedom.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple comparisons correction and cluster-defining thresholds
rubrics_metrics.description: For main contrasts of interest, parametric and categorical beauty, activation is reported at cluster-level significance (PClust-FWE < 0.05) with familywise error correction over the whole brain as reported by SPM8 based on random field theory. A statistical threshold of Punc. < 0.001 and an extent threshold of 10 voxels was used to define clusters. For other contrasts vs baseline, peak voxel threshold PFWE < 0.05 was used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define a voxelwise cluster-defining threshold (e.g., Punc<0.001), set an extent threshold, and control familywise error at the cluster level (or report PFWE for peak voxels) over the whole brain; clearly state thresholds used and rationale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conjunction-null analysis to test overlap
rubrics_metrics.description: A conjunction-null analysis (Nichols et al., 2005) was used to determine whether there was an overlap, within mOFC, in regions of parametric activation with beauty and the general de-activation produced by viewing mathematical formulae.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use formal conjunction tests to identify voxels jointly significant for multiple contrasts, referencing appropriate conjunction methodology (e.g., Nichols et al., 2005).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting coordinates and anatomical space
rubrics_metrics.description: Co-ordinates are given in Montreal Neurological Institute (MNI) space (Evans et al., 1993).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report activation peaks and cluster hotspots with coordinates and specify the stereotactic space used (MNI or Talairach).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting and interpreting de-activations
rubrics_metrics.description: The contrast All equations < Baseline revealed widespread cortical de-activations; the mOFC de-activation overlaps the mOFC activation correlating parametrically with beauty. The authors interpret relative increases in activity within a de-activated area as correlating with beauty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report de-activations as well as activations; examine overlaps between de-activation maps and task-related activations; interpret relative changes within deactivated regions carefully (e.g., an area can be deactivated relative to baseline yet show relative activation with increasing subjective rating).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting non-significant activations and limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: There were some activations which did not reach significance (clearly noted) which we nevertheless report since they suggest areas which may be contributing to the main activation. Whether they actually do will be left to future studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document subthreshold activations as potential contributors but clearly flag them as non-significant and exploratory; avoid strong claims based on non-significant results and recommend follow-up studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Behavioral data reporting and supplementary materials
rubrics_metrics.description: An excel file containing raw behavioral data is provided as Data Sheet 3: BehavioralData.xlsx, giving pre-scan beauty ratings, scan-time ratings, understanding ratings, session/trial breakdowns, and summary tables; other supplemental data sheets include the equation lists and questionnaires.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide full behavioral datasets and experimental materials as supplementary files to allow transparency, replication, and secondary analysis; tabulate ratings by subject/session/trial and include descriptive summaries and correlations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of qualitative subject questionnaires
rubrics_metrics.description: Post-scan questionnaires asked whether subjects experienced an emotional response to beautiful equations, whether they derived pleasure/satisfaction, and whether they experienced a heightened state of consciousness when contemplating a beautiful equation; responses were summarized qualitatively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include brief qualitative/self-report items to capture phenomenology of the experience; report aggregated responses and exemplar quotes when informative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretive caution about localization and network interactions
rubrics_metrics.description: Localization of activity in mOFC that correlates with the experience of mathematical beauty does not imply this area alone underlies the experience; mOFC is active in concert with other areas engaged by the specific domain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid strong claims that a single region 'is responsible' for a complex subjective experience; discuss activations in the context of broader networks and domain-specific areas.
